name: Patsch
kurzbeschreibung: Municipality in the district of Innsbruck-Land, located about 6.7 km south of Innsbruck at the foot of the Patscherkofel.
beschreibung:
Overview

Patsch is situated on the sun-blessed Southeastern Low Mountain Terrace in the Tyrolean district of Innsbruck-Land, about nine kilometres south of Innsbruck on a panoramic plateau at the foot of Mount Patscherkofel at an altitude of 998 metres. This peaceful residential community has around 1,150 inhabitants and covers an area of 9.7 square kilometres at the entrance to the Wipp Valley, high above the deep gorge of the Sill River. Thanks to its commanding vantage point, Patsch offers sweeping panoramas across the Kalkkögel peaks, the Stubai glaciers, the Inn Valley, and the Nordkette range. The village has carefully preserved its classic Tyrolean ambiance with flower-decked farmhouses and traditional alpine inns. Patsch is globally known for the majestic Europa Bridge spanning the gorge along its western boundary and for its direct access to Innsbruck's legendary Olympic mountain, the Patscherkofel.

History

Patsch possesses a rich history of human presence spanning thousands of years. On the forested Goldbichl hill within the municipal area, archaeologists uncovered a major prehistoric sanctuary and sacrificial burning site from the Bronze and Iron Ages, yielding exceptional artefacts of alpine-wide renown. The settlement was first documented in written records around 1200 under the name Patsche. Patsch is one of the oldest mother parishes in the central Inn Valley. The primary architectural landmark is the Catholic Parish Church of St. Donatus: originating in the Romanesque and Gothic eras, it was masterfully redesigned in 1767 in elegant Rococo style by the famed priest-architect Franz de Paula Penz. It preserves a magnificent reliquary shrine of Saint Donatus, revered by farmers as the protector against lightning and severe mountain storms. In the modern era, the engineering marvel of the Europa Bridge (1959–1963) and the Winter Olympic Games of 1964 and 1976 shaped its history.

Getting There

Reaching Patsch is fast and easy thanks to its proximity to Innsbruck and the Brenner transit route. By car, drive from Innsbruck via the scenic low-mountain road through Igls and Vill in roughly 15 minutes. Alternatively, travel along the Brenner Autobahn A13, taking the Patsch-Europabrücke exit, where a well-maintained road leads straight into the village centre. Rail passengers arrive at Innsbruck Central Station. From the railway station forecourt, regular VVT regional bus routes run directly to Patsch and the cable car stations at hourly intervals without transfers. Cyclists can also reach the village via the scenic cycling paths traversing the southern low-mountain plateau.

Tips

The foremost outdoor attraction is Mount Patscherkofel (2,246 m), Innsbruck's beloved local mountain. In winter, the state-of-the-art Patscherkofelbahn gondola serves sunny ski pistes, ski-touring routes, and toboggan runs. In summer, walking the celebrated Zirbenweg (Stone Pine Trail) is an absolute must: this high-altitude panorama trail meanders at over 2,000 metres above sea level through one of the oldest and largest contiguous stone pine forests in Europe from Patscherkofel to Tulfeinjöch near Tulfes. Engineering enthusiasts can admire the Europa Bridge; standing 190 metres above the valley floor, it features a commercial bungee jumping station and the Europa Chapel, decorated with frescoes by Tyrolean painter Karl Plattner. History lovers can follow the archaeological trail to the prehistoric Goldbichl sanctuary.
